_notes: screens[id].nodes = the screen read back from the page as a tree (t = button / select / input / h2 / p / text / div..., c = children, tip = hover text, hidden = not shown). actions[id] = what each menu button of that screen does: {do:"go",screen} = slide to that screen, {do:"click",id} = presses the legacy button with that id (see legacy_buttons, and overlays for the window it opens), {do:"back"}. flow = the same as one readable tree. overlays.settings.tabs = every Settings option with type, choices and default.

c.text: Split Ridge2 playersSplit Ridge2 players · Small · mountain passA mountain wall cuts the map in two. Only the north pass and the south pass lead through, each with a derrick in its mouth.
Ferry Quarter2 playersFerry Quarter2 players · Small · river cityA river splits an old city. Three bridges, street fighting on both banks, and derricks by the outer bridges.
Breakwater2–4 playersBreakwater4 players · Medium · coast · naval laneA sea lane runs through the middle from coast to coast. Two bridges cross it; ships in the lane can shell both of them.
Four Mills2–4 playersFour Mills4 players · Medium · valley · millsFour old mills in a green valley. Hill spurs split north from south; the two gaps between them hold the derricks.
Six Roads2–6 playersSix Roads6 players · Large · mixed · lake, hills, ruinsSix bases in a ring around a lake. Every neighbor shares a derrick with you, and every road ends at the lakeside.

South Lebanon2–4 playersSouth Lebanon2–4 players · green · green hills · coast · riverGreen limestone hills between the Mediterranean coast and the Litani River. Villages to fight through, ridges to hold, two river crossings. Home turf: Hezbollah & Israel.

Gulf Coast Landings2–4 playersGulf Coast Landings2–4 players · desert shore · naval-heavyBases on a desert shore above the open sea. Naval power matters. Home turf: Saudi Arabia & United Arab Emirates.

Euphrates Crossing2 playersEuphrates Crossing2 players · river · three bridges · river towns · duelA duel across the Euphrates: three bridges, a river town guarding each bank and marshes that funnel the armor. Home turf: Hezbollah & Iran & Kataib Hezbollah.

Yemen: Tihama and Highlands2 playersYemen: Tihama and Highlands2 players · desert · coastal plains · highland diamond · wadisHot coastal plains on both sides and a rugged highland diamond in the middle with the old capital inside. The wadi passes along the middle are the only easy way in; the ridge corners are for snipers and artillery. Home turf: Ansarallah & Saudi Arabia.

Zagros: Mountain Fortress2 playersZagros: Mountain Fortress2 players · mountain ranges · three valleysTwo snow-capped ranges split the land into three valleys. Armies fight for the mountain passes. Home turf: Iran.

Caribbean Island2 playersCaribbean Island2 players · green · tropical island · beaches · naval-heavyA long tropical island in warm seas: Havana on the north shore, palm-fringed cays and landings on the beaches.

Strait of Hormuz: Island Gate2 playersStrait of Hormuz: Island Gate2 players · desert · sea strait · island chain · two coasts · naviesThe narrow strait between the Iranian and Arabian coasts, wide gulf at both ends and a chain of three islands in the narrows. Bridges hop island to island; fleets fight for the water, tanks for the causeways. Home turf: Iran & United Arab Emirates.

Taiwan Strait2 playersTaiwan Strait2 players · green · sea strait · island · naval-heavyMainland China faces the island across the strait. Two long military causeways can be stormed, but navies, landing craft and air power decide who lands where. Home turf: China & Japan.

Arctic Front: Frozen Armies2 playersArctic Front: Frozen Armies2 players · snow & ice · frozen river · forests · rocky hillsA frozen river and snowbound forests. Three bridges, rocky hills and falling snow.

Khyber Pass: Gate of Fortresses2 playersKhyber Pass: Gate of Fortresses2 players · mountain pass · two goat tracks · duelA duel through the Spin Ghar range: one narrow pass split by a rock fort in the middle, and a long goat track along each edge to outflank it. Home turf: Pakistan.

Hajar Mountains: Wadi Passes2 playersHajar Mountains: Wadi Passes2 players · desert · bare mountains · deep wadis · oasis fortsThe Hajar range: bare mountains cut by deep wadis, oasis villages with old forts and a single paved pass over the top. Pass control is everything. Home turf: United Arab Emirates & Iran.

Southern Marshes2 playersSouthern Marshes2 players · green · reed marsh · lagoons · causeways · villagesThe great southern marshes: reed islands and shallow lagoons, canoe villages and narrow causeways. Few roads, many ambush lanes; the island market town in the middle supplies the winner. Home turf: Kataib Hezbollah & Iran.

Black Sea Coast: Green Mountains2 playersBlack Sea Coast: Green Mountains2 players · green · wet green mountains · tea slopes · coast road · naviesThe rainy north coast of Turkey: forested mountains with tea terraces dropping to a port-lined coast road, small valleys and ships offshore. Everything is narrow and green. Home turf: Turkey & Russia & Ukraine.

Yemen Highlands4 playersYemen Highlands4 players · mountains · coast · narrow passesFrom the Red Sea coast up into the Sarawat mountains: tower-house cities of the highlands, narrow passes and a port on the plain. Home turf: Ansarallah & Saudi Arabia.

Hawizeh Marshes4 playersHawizeh Marshes4 players · green · marshland · causeway crossroadsThe reed marshes on the Iran-Iraq border: a lagoon in the middle crossed by two causeways that meet on an island, and marsh pools that channel every advance. Home turf: Iran & Hezbollah & Kataib Hezbollah.

Island Chain Armada4 playersIsland Chain Armada4 players · island chain · naval-heavyFour island fortresses around a central isle in open sea. Long bridges are the only land routes, so fleets decide the war.

Donbas Steppe4 playersDonbas Steppe4 players · green · open fields · two rivers · mining towns · autumn mudThe open black-earth steppe of eastern Ukraine: two meandering rivers, slag-heap hills and mining towns around a big crossroads town. Best in autumn mud, when only the roads move fast. Home turf: Ukraine & Russia.

Mesopotamia4 playersMesopotamia4 players · two rivers · citiesIraq between the Tigris and the Euphrates: Baghdad between the rivers, Basra by the Shatt al-Arab and bridges everywhere. Home turf: Iran & Hezbollah & Kataib Hezbollah.

Persian Plateau4 playersPersian Plateau4 players · high desert · salt lake · mountain passesIran's high desert below the Alborz range: a salt lake in the middle, cities on the old caravan road and three mountain passes to the north. Home turf: Iran.

Siberian Taiga4 playersSiberian Taiga4 players · snow & ice · snow forest · frozen lakes · hillsDeep winter in the taiga: frozen lakes and wooded hills break the snow into lanes, with a logging town in the middle worth holding. Home turf: Russia.

Aegean Islands6 playersAegean Islands6 players · green · sea · island bridges · navyTwo coasts facing each other across the Aegean. Two islands carry bridges across the sea; the rock in the middle belongs to whoever rules the waves. Home turf: Turkey & United Kingdom & France.

Korean DMZ: Iron Triangle6 playersKorean DMZ: Iron Triangle6 players · green · hills · two rivers · fortified strip · winterThe narrow demilitarized strip between two rivers, studded with fortified hills, and a wooded ridge on each flank. Armies cross by a few bridges under artillery cover. Best in winter snow. Home turf: South Korea & North Korea.

Empty Quarter Edge6 playersEmpty Quarter Edge6 players · desert · giant dunes · sabkha flats · oil roadThe edge of the Empty Quarter: giant dunes, salt flats you can cross and dunes you cannot, a gravel road with oil camps. Open, fast and brutal on fuel. Home turf: Saudi Arabia & United Arab Emirates & Ansarallah.
Oasis Basin: Last Water6–8 playersOasis Basin: Last Water6–8 players · open desert · central lakeOpen desert ringed around a central lake. No bridges, many approaches.

Pacific Atolls6–8 playersPacific Atolls6–8 players · ocean · island bases · offshore oil · big naviesEight island bases ring a great ocean. Bridges link neighbors around the ring and to the central isle; rock-pad oil rigs sit in open water between them, and fleets and landings decide who holds them.

Hindu Kush8 playersHindu Kush8 players · snow & ice · eight valleys · central massif · ring roadEight valleys around a snow massif. Ridges wall each valley off from the next, so armies meet on the road around the mountain - or go round the outside. Home turf: Pakistan & Iran.

Burning Oil Fields: Inferno8 playersBurning Oil Fields: Inferno8 players · eight-way war · oil field in the middleEight armies around a great oil field in the open desert. The derricks in the middle pay the most; rock outcrops between the bases cover the approaches. Home turf: Saudi Arabia & United Arab Emirates.

Rhine Front8 playersRhine Front8 players · green · river · four bridges · forest hills · four a sideFour armies on each bank of the Rhine: four bridges, river towns, and forested hills that hide flanking moves. Home turf: Germany & France & United Kingdom.

Yangtze Gorges8 playersYangtze Gorges8 players · green · great river · four bridges · gorge hillsThe Yangtze cuts the map in two between steep gorge hills. Four bridges, towns at both ends of the middle ones, four bases on each bank. Home turf: China.

Sinai: Iron Mesa8 playersSinai: Iron Mesa8 players · dry highlands · rock mesas · no waterDry highlands with rock mesas and no water. A pure land war: the mesas split the plateau into lanes around a big central butte. Home turf: Egypt.

c.text: IRIranAsymmetric Warfare · morale: ZealousDoctrine: Asymmetric Warfare (infantry, AT teams and drones holding still or in cover deal 20% more damage; infantry and light vehicles sprint 25% faster for 3s after firing). Morale style: Zealous - Slow to break; fervor rises as comrades fall and banners rally the faithful. They hold their ground, so they take heavier losses. Missiles & cheap drones: Shahed drones cost 25% less and build almost twice as fast, Fateh missile launchers fire 12% farther and hit 15% harder, the Kheibar barrage charges faster. Tunnel warfare: hidden tunnels move units across the map instantly.Special: IRGC Field Commander · thermoStrike: Kheibar Missile Strike

HezbollahFortress & Ambush · morale: ZealousDoctrine: Fortress & Ambush (infantry, AT teams and drones holding still or in cover deal 20% more damage; +15% damage near their own buildings). Morale style: Zealous - Slow to break; fervor rises as comrades fall and banners rally the faithful. They hold their ground, so they take heavier losses. The Lebanese mountain Shia resistance: stone villages of Bint Jbeil and the Bekaa, Ashura banners and Ya Hussein walls, rocket barrages, cheap strong drones, ATGM ambush teams, tunnels and mountain forts. Longer-ranged rockets that fire faster, far stronger Defense Guns and tunnels, infantry whose dugouts take 30% less damage. No air force or navy. Tunnel warfare: hidden tunnels move units across the map instantly.Special: Mountain Rocket Team · bunkersStrike: Mountain Rocket Storm

AnsarallahDesert Raiders · morale: ZealousDoctrine: Desert Raiders (infantry, AT teams and drones holding still or in cover deal 20% more damage; infantry and light vehicles sprint 25% faster for 3s after firing). Morale style: Zealous - Slow to break; fervor rises as comrades fall and banners rally the faithful. They hold their ground, so they take heavier losses. Yemeni highland raiders: tower-house towns of Sana'a and the Sarawat, coffee terraces and Red Sea coast. Tough, fast armed technicals and long-range rocket trucks that outrange enemy artillery. Units move 13% faster and cost 8% less. No air force. Tunnel warfare: hidden tunnels move units across the map instantly.Special: Raid Leader Technical · camoStrike: Long-Range Rocket Salvo

Kataib HezbollahDefense of the Shrines · morale: ZealousDoctrine: Defense of the Shrines (infantry, AT teams and drones holding still or in cover deal 20% more damage; +15% damage near their own buildings). Morale style: Zealous - Slow to break; fervor rises as comrades fall and banners rally the faithful. They hold their ground, so they take heavier losses. Volunteer brigades of the south, defenders of the shrines: infantry cost 18% less and train faster, units ambush hard from cover and fight 15% harder near their own buildings, and they never rout. Mixed militia and state-issued gear. Hidden Firing Posts: cheap small posts that stay hidden until they fire (no tunnel network).Special: Marsh Scout Team · crewsStrike: Grad Salvo

OBHamasUrban Labyrinth · morale: ZealousDoctrine: Urban Labyrinth (infantry, AT teams and drones holding still or in cover deal 20% more damage; +15% damage near their own buildings). Morale style: Zealous - Slow to break; fervor rises as comrades fall and banners rally the faithful. They hold their ground, so they take heavier losses. Hamas, a light urban resistance force of a dense coastal city: rifle squads, RPG and ATGM teams, snipers and mortars, armed technicals, home-made rocket trucks and quadcopter drone teams. No tanks, jets, helicopters or warships. Cheap infantry (cost 15% less) fight from hidden firing posts and rubble ambush positions, hitting 20% harder from cover and 15% harder near their own buildings. Zealous: they never rout, but they pay in heavy losses and thin armor. Hidden Firing Posts: cheap small posts that stay hidden until they fire (no tunnel network).Special: Rooftop Observers · crewsStrike: Rocket Salvo

USUnited StatesAggressive Maneuver · morale: ProfessionalDoctrine: Aggressive Maneuver (+15% damage while advancing or attacking; vehicles 10% faster). Morale style: Professional - Steady under artillery and quick to rally near officers; heavy losses sap them more than other armies. Air power & precision: weapons deal 8% more damage; F-35s and Apaches hit 25% harder and are tougher.Special: Delta Operator · trainingStrike: Tomahawk Salvo

GBUnited KingdomCombined Arms · morale: ProfessionalDoctrine: Combined Arms (+15% damage near their own buildings). Morale style: Professional - Steady under artillery and quick to rally near officers; heavy losses sap them more than other armies. British Armed Forces, combined arms: infantry train 15% faster and cost 10% less, Challenger tanks cost 10% less, and units fight 10% harder on home ground.Special: Royal Marines Recon Troop · crewsStrike: Typhoon Strike

FRFranceArmée de Terre · morale: ProfessionalDoctrine: Armée de Terre (+15% damage near their own buildings). Morale style: Professional - Steady under artillery and quick to rally near officers; heavy losses sap them more than other armies. Artillerie & génie: units self-repair, structures have 30% more hit points, all units cost 3% less, CAESAR guns hit 15% harder.Special: Équipe MMP Longue Portée · networkStrike: SCALP Salvo

DEGermanyPanzertruppe · morale: ProfessionalDoctrine: Panzertruppe (+15% damage near their own buildings). Morale style: Professional - Steady under artillery and quick to rally near officers; heavy losses sap them more than other armies. Panzertruppe & Heer: units self-repair, structures have 30% more hit points, all units cost 3% less, PzH 2000 guns hit 15% harder.Special: Jägerzug Panzerabwehr · networkStrike: Taurus Salvo

ILIsraelCovert Operations · morale: Firepower-reliantDoctrine: Covert Operations (infantry and AT teams are camouflaged; first shot from hiding hits 50% harder). Morale style: Firepower-reliant - Lowest morale: they break sooner, especially with no armor, artillery or air support nearby. Balanced by stronger fire support and sturdier modern gear. Iron Dome & missile defense: units are 10% tougher, hit 5% harder and cost 4% less, enemy strikes and missiles do 50% damage to you, SAM sites reach 30% farther and hit harder, Merkava tanks are extra tough, Spike missiles hit hard.Special: Iron Dome Battery · trophyStrike: Air Strike

UAUkraineHomeland Defense · morale: Home defendersDoctrine: Homeland Defense (infantry and light vehicles sprint 25% faster for 3s after firing; +15% damage near their own buildings). Drone war & resilience: FPV drones are cheap and build fast, Sea Baby drone boats hit 40% harder, units repair themselves out of combat, forces cost 4% less.Special: Aerorozvidka Drone Team · salvageStrike: Neptune Missile Salvo

Heavy armor & massed artillery: vehicles have 45% more hit points, artillery is tougher and hits 15% harder. TOS-1A burns everything nearby.Special: Krasukha EW Truck · reactiveStrike: Iskander Strike

CNChinaMass & Information War · morale: ProfessionalDoctrine: Mass & Information War (artillery reaches 15% farther, bigger blasts, faster reloads, 15% cheaper; shellfire suppresses harder). Morale style: Professional - Steady under artillery and quick to rally near officers; heavy losses sap them more than other armies. Mass mobilization & blue-water navy: infantry cost 42% less and train 40% faster, everything else costs 5% less, warships are 30% tougher and hit 15% harder, rocket artillery hits 10% harder.Special: PLA Political Commissar · nationalismStrike: DF-21 Strike

Morale style: Zealous - Slow to break; fervor rises as comrades fall and banners rally the faithful. They hold their ground, so they take heavier losses. Numbers & artillery: everything costs 20% less but units have 10% fewer hit points; Koksan guns cost 20% less and fire 10% farther. Tunnel warfare: hidden tunnels move units across the map instantly.Special: Bureau 121 Hackers · conscriptStrike: Hwasong Strike

c.text: Test range now opens a small window: choose your nation, the target nation (it can be the same one) and a map, then Start. Inside the range, "Change nations…" in the Test range box restarts it with a new pair, no trip through the main menu.

Build a Generator (Build tab, about the price of a Barracks) to power your electronic buildings: air defense, coastal missiles, the Strike Center, Radio & TV, the Airfield and your minimap radar. Your top bar shows power produced and used: green is fine, red means LOW POWER and those buildings go offline until you build another Generator or capture a map power plant. Barracks, War Factory, Depot and defense guns never need power. Blowing up enemy Generators is a real tactic.
Every building has its own queue

Like Generals: infantry come only from a Barracks, vehicles from a War Factory, aircraft from an Airfield, ships from a Shipyard. Select the building to see what it can make and its own queue (progress bar on the first unit, ×3 badges). Click = add one, Shift+click = add five, right-click a queued icon = cancel one with a full refund. Two Barracks build two soldiers at the same time; each unit walks out of its own building to that building's rally point. With nothing selected the Units tab still works and picks the least busy building. A destroyed building refunds its queue. The old +50% speed for a second building is gone.
One game: Battle, now with supply lines

The game is now one game: Battle (Command Center, supply trucks, tech tree, destroy every enemy building). Conquest and the Grand campaign are gone. Battle has SUPPLY LINES: the roads running out of your Command Center and Supply Depots are green on the minimap (L shows them on the ground). Units refill ammo near your buildings and on those roads; far beyond them they fight until empty, then must come back or get an Ammo Truck from the War Factory. Craters, blown bridges and enemy checkpoints cut a line (dashed) - your Construction Vehicle repairs a crater fast. Every old battlefield is now a Battle map, and the main menu is Play · Multiplayer · Test range.
The main menu shows your war
The main menu background now shows whatever Continue would take you back to: that battlefield with your front line drawn in.
Every button says what it beats

Unit buttons now carry two small pictures: green = what this unit BEATS best, red = what it is most WEAK TO. Hold the mouse on a button for the full list with names. Point at an enemy unit (or select it) and the buttons that beat it light up green with "BEATS IT". The game works these out from the real damage, armor, range and price numbers against the nation you are fighting, so they are always true - the Encyclopedia and the Unit guide show the same.

Every report from the field - base under attack, enemy spotted, unit lost, building finished, a unit ready - is now one short line with a small icon at the top left of the battle (three lines at most, each fades after a few seconds). Lines marked with a small arrow know where it happened: click the line, or press Space, and the camera goes there. Settings has a switch for it.

When something happens away from where you are looking - your base or troops come under attack, a unit is lost, a unit or building is finished, a teammate pings the map - a small round marker with an arrow now sits on the edge of the screen pointing at it for about six seconds (three at most). Click it and the camera goes there. Settings has a switch for it.

The sound is mixed properly now: even the biggest fight no longer crackles or distorts, unit voices stay clear over the guns (explosions and music step back a little while a soldier speaks), every button and menu item gives a soft click, and each battlefield has a quiet background of its own - dry desert wind, wind in the trees, or a thin winter howl - with the muffled thump of fighting elsewhere on the map.

Every nation now fights with one of four styles: Zealous (slow to break, banners rally the faithful, heavier losses), Professional (steady under artillery, rally fast near officers), Home defenders (much braver on home turf) and Firepower-reliant (break sooner, but stronger fire support). The style shows on the nation pick screen and in the Encyclopedia.
